title: The Return of Repair
source: AI-generated original passage. IELTS-style practice; no published test text reproduced.
passageHtml:
A For much of the twentieth century, repairing household objects was ordinary. Shoes were resoled, radios were opened and mended, and furniture was expected to last. In recent decades, however, many products have become cheaper to replace than to fix. The result is not only more waste but also a loss of practical knowledge about how things work.

B Repair cafés, community workshops where volunteers help people mend broken items, have appeared in many countries as a response. Visitors bring lamps, toys, clothing or small appliances and work alongside someone with relevant skills. The aim is not simply to provide a free repair service. Organisers often insist that owners participate, because learning to diagnose a fault is part of the benefit.

C The movement challenges a common assumption about consumers. People are often described as choosing convenience over durability, but the popularity of repair events suggests a more complex picture. Many owners feel attached to objects because of memory, design or dislike of waste. A repaired object can carry a story that a new purchase does not.

D Manufacturers sometimes argue that repair is unsafe or uneconomic. Modern devices may contain sealed batteries, glued screens or specialised screws, making home repair difficult. Some companies say these features protect users or improve performance. Critics respond that such design choices also restrict independent repair and shorten the useful life of products.

E Governments have begun to consider “right to repair” rules. These may require companies to provide spare parts, manuals or diagnostic information for a certain number of years. The details matter. A rule that technically permits repair but prices parts too highly will have little effect. Similarly, information that is available only to authorised centres may not help community repairers or ordinary owners.

F Repair is unlikely to reverse mass consumption by itself. It can be slow, and some products are genuinely beyond saving. Yet repair culture changes the question people ask. Instead of asking only whether a product is new or cheap, they may ask whether it can be opened, understood and maintained. That shift could influence design, purchasing habits and the skills people value.

questions.question: In the past, repairing everyday objects was unusual.
questions.reason_ja: 本文Aでは、20世紀の多くの時期に家庭用品の修理は ordinary（普通）だったと述べています。設問の unusual はこれと矛盾します。

questions.question: Repair cafés usually ask visitors to help with the repair process.
questions.evidence: Organisers often insist that owners participate
questions.reason_ja: 本文Bでは、主催者は所有者が participate することを重視すると述べています。修理をただ受け取るのではなく、一緒に関わるという内容です。

questions.question: All repair café volunteers are professional engineers.
questions.evidence: volunteers help people mend broken items
questions.reason_ja: volunteers がいること、関連スキルを持つ人がいることは本文にあります。しかし「全員が専門エンジニア」とは述べられていないため NOT GIVEN です。
questions.not_given_reason: 本文は volunteers と relevant skills について述べますが、全員が professional engineers であるとは書かれていません。

questions.question: The popularity of repair events suggests that consumers may care about more than convenience.
questions.evidence: the popularity of repair events suggests a more complex picture.
questions.reason_ja: 本文Cでは、消費者は単に便利さだけを選ぶという見方に対し、修理イベントの人気はより複雑な実態を示すと述べています。記憶やデザイン、廃棄への嫌悪も理由になります。

questions.question: Manufacturers and critics agree that sealed batteries make repair easier.
questions.evidence: sealed batteries... making home repair difficult.
questions.reason_ja: 本文Dでは、sealed batteries などが home repair を difficult にすると述べています。設問は easier としており本文と逆です。

questions.question: Right to repair rules are always effective once they are introduced.
questions.evidence: A rule that technically permits repair but prices parts too highly will have little effect.
questions.reason_ja: 本文Eでは、修理を認める規則があっても部品が高すぎれば効果は小さいと述べています。always effective という断定が本文に反します。

questions.question: Complete the summary. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.
questions.summaryHtml: Repair cafés are not designed only as a {{20|Q20}} service. They encourage owners to learn how to {{21|Q21}} a fault. Some manufacturers use sealed parts or specialised screws, which may limit {{22|Q22}} repair. Right to repair laws may fail if spare parts are priced too {{23|Q23}}.

evidence.20: The aim is not simply to provide a free repair service.
evidence.21: learning to diagnose a fault is part of the benefit.
evidence.22: such design choices also restrict independent repair

reason_ja.20: 本文Bの not simply to provide a free repair service が対応します。repair cafés は無料修理だけが目的ではありません。
reason_ja.21: 故障箇所を見つけることを diagnose a fault と表しています。本文中の語を使うので diagnose が答えです。
reason_ja.22: 本文Dでは、設計上の選択が independent repair を restrict すると述べています。limit は restrict の言い換えです。
reason_ja.23: 本文Eの prices parts too highly に対応します。副詞として highly が本文語です。

questions.question: Which paragraph explains why repaired objects may have emotional value?
questions.evidence: Many owners feel attached to objects because of memory, design or dislike of waste.
questions.reason_ja: C段落では、所有者が記憶やデザイン、廃棄を避けたい気持ちから物に愛着を持つと述べています。emotional value は feel attached の言い換えです。

questions.question: Which paragraph discusses how legal measures may be weakened by practical details?
questions.evidence: The details matter. A rule... prices parts too highly will have little effect.
questions.reason_ja: E段落では right to repair の規則について、部品価格や情報アクセスの条件によって実効性が変わると述べています。legal measures may be weakened が little effect に対応します。

questions.question: The writer’s main conclusion is that repair culture may change how people evaluate products.
questions.evidence: they may ask whether it can be opened, understood and maintained.
questions.reason_ja: 最終段落では、修理文化によって「新しいか・安いか」だけでなく「開けられるか、理解できるか、維持できるか」を問うようになると述べています。製品評価の基準が変わるという内容なので TRUE です。
